notes: RELEASE ... FROM is 'equivalent to the execution of' MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1 'according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement' and then RELEASE (§1985:XI.4.2.4 GR3). SortBinder#BindRelease hands the FROM operand to MoveBinder#BindFromPhrase, which checks the record-area overlap and the function class and builds the implicit move with the one MOVE binder (BindMoveOf), so the MOVE legality and conversion rules apply unchanged; SortEmitter#EmitRelease emits that move before the release; VersionConformancePass#VisitRecordFromPhrase refuses the 2023 FROM literal-1 at 85 (COBOL0871). Probes at 85: group record from shorter (space pad), longer and reference-modified (1:7)/(4:7)/(10:1) senders, signed S9(3) -12 (bytes 01K moved unconverted to a group), numeric-edited and an alphanumeric function all match MOVE; elementary S9(5) record from -12.5 (-00012), "00042" (+00042), 18 digits (truncated +45678) and de-edited ZZ9.9 "  7.5" (+00007, §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR4); numeric-edited record -ZZ9.99; an ODO record from an ODO group gives the same bytes as the plain MOVE. Refused: alphabetic to numeric and noninteger to alphanumeric (COBOL0819), literal, figurative and SPACE operands (COBOL0871), numeric function (COBOL1914), FROM the record itself (COBOL6827), empty and doubled FROM. The witness releases two 7-character items into a 5-character group record and returns them truncated.

next.reason: §2023:14.9.32.4 GR4 keeps the MOVE-then-RELEASE equivalence and adds 'MOVE literal-1 TO record-name-1' for the new FROM literal-1 form, which the 1985 format lacks. §2023:14.9.32.3 SR3 states the MOVE-validity part ('shall be valid as a sending operand in a MOVE statement'). The added undefined-result sentence and the overlap NOTE follow from the MOVE equivalence. A 1985 RELEASE FROM identifier means the same; the rule is looser.
